Hi Kelsey,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to kick off the private deployment workstream and I wanted to confirm a few scope items before we loop in engineering:

- VPC peering vs. PrivateLink: you mentioned preference for VPC peering in the shoebox notes, but we'll need confirmation if PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is required for tighter egress controls.
- HSM/KMS integration: do you require our HSM-backed KMS integration or will Arcadia use a customer-managed KMS?
- On‑prem package: are you planning an air-gapped install for any datacenter locations, or will all nodes be in cloud VPCs?

Can you attach the simple network sketch you shared during the call (subnets, NAT/GW, egress inspection points) so we can validate the acceptance checklist? I'm proposing a 60-minute kickoff with engineering on Wed — please let me know availability.

I've copied Tom for visibility.

Best,

Hi Soojin,

Thanks — attached is the sketch we used. Quick answers below:

- We prefer VPC peering for primary traffic, but some teams want an interface endpoint option for sensitive telemetry. We can do peering first and circle back on endpoints.
- KMS: Arcadia will provide a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS with a customer key). We do not need HSM for the initial rollout, but will request HSM support in a future phase.
- On‑prem: Not full air-gap. We have one colo site in us-west-2 where the appliance will live behind a restricted egress proxy; installer will need outbound access to Redwood's package registry on a tightly scoped allowlist.

We can do Wed 11:00am PT for the kickoff.

Thanks,

Thanks for the details. I reviewed the sketch and drafted a short VPC acceptance checklist (attached). High level notes:

1) Peering topology: Peering is fine for high-throughput inference traffic. Confirm route table entries do not overlap; recommend /16 customer VPCs be split to avoid overlap with Redwood test ranges.

2) MTU & fragmentation: If they run NAT Instances or appliances in colo, confirm end-to-end MTU >= 1400 to avoid tokenization issues on large payloads.

3) DNS & Private endpoints: If they add an interface endpoint for telemetry, require private DNS delegation or conditional forwarders to ensure SDK resolves regional endpoints to private IPs.

4) KMS: customer-managed AWS KMS is supported; we need the key ARN and a cross-account IAM role with kms:Decrypt permission during setup. No HSM for phase 1.

5) Egress allowlist: Provide the following minimal set: registry.redwoodinference.com:443, telemetry-ingest.redwoodinference.com:443, package-updates.redwoodinference.com:443. If their proxy requires IP allowlist, we can provide a signed manifest.

6) Monitoring & metrics: we’ll expose a read-only metrics endpoint on port 9100; please confirm NACL/SG rules allow outbound 9100/https to our monitoring collector if they choose the private endpoint route.

Next steps: I attached vpc-acceptance-template.xlsx — can we populate this with Arcadia's VPC IDs and subnets before the kickoff? Also recommend a 30-minute pre-call between our network engineer and Arcadia's infra lead (Tom) tomorrow 10:00am PT to walk the sketch.

Attachment: vpc-acceptance-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
